articles.title: Volvo research shows automaker has decreased injury for men and women by 79%
articles.author: Teresa Moss

paras.en: A new report from Volvo finds that equal protection for men and women can be achieved through data-driven safety development grounded in real-world crash research, the release states.
The research found that overall injury for drivers has decreased by 79% for Volvo models from 2010 to 2019 compared to models from 1970 to 1979.
Volvo saw an 88% decrease for women, bringing the injury risk to the same level as men, the release states.

“The results also show substantial advances in occupant protection across all seating positions,” the release adds. “Restrained rear-seat occupants in Volvo cars benefit from protection levels comparable to, and in some cases exceeding, those of front-seat occupants.”

Volvo says the data underscores the effectiveness of decades of rear-seat safety innovation in Volvo cars. This happened with the lack of regulatory requirements and standardized testing, the release states.

“For too long, safety in the automotive industry has not worked equally well for everyone,” says Åsa Haglund, Volvo head of Cars Safety Centre, in the release. “At Volvo Cars, we’ve taken a different approach. By studying real-world crashes and designing with the needs of women, men and children of all body types in mind, we’ve worked for decades to provide a high level of protection regardless of who you are or where you sit in the car. Our latest research confirms that equal protection is not just an ambition, but something we have been able to achieve in Volvo cars for many years.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Volvo has collected data since 1970 from more than 50,000 real-world crashes involving more than 80,000 occupants, the release notes. It adds that the insights are translated into safety requirements, testing, vehicle development, verification, and production.
“The result is a continuous cycle of learning that helps drive innovations and improve protection for everyone,” according to the release.
The study also reviewed different crash types. It found that frontal impact injuries were reduced by 79% for all drivers. Side impacts saw a larger reduction in injuries at 89%.

The approach also laid the foundation for pioneering Volvo Cars Safety Standard, according to the release. Through the standard, Volvo sets its own benchmark for real-world safety, going beyond regulation or safety ratings, Volvo says.

“And because real-world crashes don’t involve standardized crash test dummies, Volvo Cars’ research involves considering a diverse range of occupant characteristics, including gender, height, body shape and weight,” the release states. “As a result, the company’s safety innovations are designed with the same diversity in mind.”

Volvo notes it has openly shared its safety research to help raise safety standards across the industry through the Equal Vehicles for All (E.V.A.) initiative launched in 2019. It adds that more than 50 years of safety research is freely accessible in a digital library. Carmakers, researchers and policyholders can use the data to build on Volvo’s insights.

The recent study focuses on a broad range of real-world crash scenarios, including frontal, side, and rear-end impacts; run-off-road collisions; rollovers; side-swipe collisions; large animal impacts; and multi-collision crashes.

It also focuses on belted occupants aged 13 or older and examines injuries with moderate potential to threaten life, such as fractures and concussions, while excluding minor injuries such as bruises and pain.
Earlier this year, Volvo introduced a new seatbelt that adapts to traffic variations and the person wearing it via real-time data.
The Volvo EX60 was the first vehicle equipped with the multi-adaptive seatbelt.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) released research in January that found women are at higher risk of injury than men in collisions. The research followed details released by the U.S. Department of Transportation on an advanced female crash test dummy.

articles.title: Hunter Updates HawkEye XL Commercial Alignment System
articles.author: Alex Crissey

paras.en: Hunter Engineering announced four new enhancements to its HawkEye XL Commercial Alignment System.
The new enhancements include (with descriptions by the company):

1) Magnetic wheel adapters – These adapters provide increased wheel protection, with no metal spades to get between the rim and tire, the company says. The adapters are available as an option for new and existing HawkEyeXL aligners.

2) Drive-through sensor configuration – The new configuration will allow drive-through shops and OEM production to skip repositioning their equipment for each alignment. The sensors offer the same long-range vision and field of view, with up to 16-foot-wide tower spacing to accommodate commercial vehicles.

3) New WinAlign software – Hunter’s latest WinAlign 18.3 software offers new target placement guidance to help the technician, aligner placement guidance so the cameras can easily see all the wheel targets, and the flexibility to perform thrustline and frame-reference alignments as desired.

4) Latest-generation alignment cart – Technicians can store adapters and control the alignment system from the rear of the vehicles. The cart is completely untethered with a battery backup, allowing a full day’s work without carrying a cable around the shop, the company says.
The XL handles heavy-duty, medium-duty, light-duty and passenger vehicles.

articles.title: MotoRad CEO Matt Buchholz on Aligning Values
articles.author: Mary DellaValle

paras.en: This episode of DriveTime features Matt Buchholz, CEO of MotoRad. In this interview, Buchholz described how the company’s D.R.I.V.E. core values — Dedication, Relationship, Innovation, Value Driven and Expertise — provide the cultural foundation for how its team operates internally and engages with customers and channel partners.

Buchholz emphasized that culture and strategy are closely connected. By aligning teams around common values and empowering employees to live them every day, he said MotoRad creates a foundation for continuous improvement — reflecting his philosophy that when an organization gets better, it gets bigger.

As MotoRad expands across thermal management, emissions and powertrain controls, Buchholz said investment decisions begin with market intelligence and listening directly to customers. The company looks for opportunities that fit its existing capabilities and strategy while addressing clear market needs. Buchholz said it also evaluates adjacent categories for “low friction” opportunities where it can create value quickly. In many cases, some of MotoRad’s strongest product ideas have originated with technicians, counter professionals and other customers who identify ways the company can improve a product or make a repair easier.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Looking ahead, Buchholz said MotoRad’s growth strategy centers on three areas: commercial execution, operational agility and technology. Commercially, the company plans to continue listening to the market, responding faster and creating greater value through areas such as coverage, service, business intelligence and quality. Operationally, MotoRad is focused on diversifying its global supply chain to maintain continuity of supply and become nimbler. Technology supports both priorities by improving efficiency, reducing waste and helping the company respond to rapidly increasing expectations for speed.

paras.en: Buchholz also sees continued opportunity for the broader aftermarket as vehicle miles traveled and vehicle age increase and vehicle technologies across thermal management, emissions and powertrain controls become more complex. “We get to support this incredibly essential business that people enjoy,” he said.

articles.title: Battery Thermal Management Market to Hit $10.97B by 2033
articles.author: Mary DellaValle

paras.en: The battery thermal management system (BTMS) market is projected to grow from $5.26 billion in 2026 to $10.97 billion by 2033 at a CAGR of 11.1%, according to MarketsandMarkets. Increasing battery energy density, fast-charging requirements, higher power output, and stringent battery safety requirements are driving value and technology intensity in BTMS.

OEMs are transitioning from conventional air cooling toward liquid-cooled and integrated thermal architectures to manage battery temperature with greater precision and efficiency. Technology is also shifting toward AI-based thermal simulation, cell-level temperature monitoring, direct cell cooling, and intelligent controls, particularly for high-voltage 800V EV platforms requiring faster charging and tighter thermal uniformity. 800V BTMS solutions are being developed with higher coolant flow, faster preconditioning, and integrated battery heating and cooling to manage higher charging loads, according to the MarketsandMarkets report.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: MAHLE Expands Battery Cooling Plate Production in Spain

In June 2026, MAHLE started series production of battery cooling plates at its Montblanc plant in Spain to support growing demand for liquid-cooled battery systems. The company plans to increase production from around 1,000 units per week to 8,000 units per week by the end of 2026, with the facility capable of reaching up to 15,000 units per week.

The cooling plates use optimized coolant channels to distribute heat uniformly across the battery and maintain operating temperatures below 40°C. MAHLE is also expanding the production area by around 10,000 m², supporting higher-volume production of battery thermal management components.
Webasto Develops Heated Chiller for Integrated Thermal Management

In December 2025, Webasto developed its Heated Chiller to combine battery cooling, battery heating, and cabin heating within a single thermal management unit. The system integrates the chiller, battery heater, and interior heater, reducing component count and simplifying thermal system integration.

The architecture supports coordinated temperature control across the battery and cabin, enabling battery preconditioning for charging while also meeting cabin heating requirements. Webasto is positioning the Heated Chiller as a compact thermal management solution for electric vehicles, with the technology progressing toward production applications.
BEV Segment Expected to Lead Global BTMS Market

The BEV segment is expected to have the largest share in the global BTMS market. BEVs are expected to be the fastest-growing vehicle type, as they account for more than 50% globally, supported by higher battery energy density, tighter cell temperature-control requirements, and greater integration of battery and vehicle thermal systems.

Within passenger BEVs, NMC batteries require active thermal control as higher energy density and charging power increase heat generation and cell temperature variation. This supports liquid cooling, direct cell cooling, battery preconditioning, and active temperature control. OEMs and BTMS suppliers are focusing on integrated and actively controlled thermal architectures.

For instance, the Mercedes AMG GT 4-Door Coupe uses direct cooling of cylindrical NCMA battery cells, with intelligent thermal management controlling cell temperature during high-power operation, while Bosch provides intelligent battery temperature control and diagnostics for BEVs.

These developments are increasing the need for optimized coolant distribution, low-thermal-resistance cooling structures, and coordinated thermal control across the battery, heat pump, HVAC, electric motor, and power electronics. High energy density batteries and higher charging power are supporting demand for advanced active BTMS solutions, particularly for NMC-based passenger BEVs.

articles.title: WAI Global Expands Late-Model Aftermarket Coverage
articles.author: Jeff White

paras.en: WAI Global expanded late-model aftermarket coverage to address evolving vehicle and application needs. In the third quarter of 2026, WAI Global introduced 124 new part numbers. These additions provide 100% new coverage for more than 52.3 million vehicles in operation across the United States and Canada.

The third-quarter introductions broaden WAI Global’s aftermarket portfolio across several key product categories. These include alternators, starters, wiper motors, window regulators, voltage regulators, brake calipers, solenoids, sensors and motors. The additions address coverage gaps, improve parts availability and support changing aftermarket demand.

“Our NPI strategy remains focused on identifying meaningful coverage gaps and bringing late-model and first-to-market solutions to customers quickly,” said Ron Bernstein, president, North America, WAI Global. “Adding coverage for more than 52 million vehicles this quarter reflects the scale of that effort and helps our customers stay ahead of changing vehicle populations and replacement demand.”
Notable late-model releases introduced during the quarter include:
- 30884N Starter: Up to 2026 Subaru Impreza

- WPM5036 Wiper Motor: Up to 2026 Hyundai Santa Fe and Tucson

articles.title: Automotive Parts Headquarters Raises $513K for WACOSA
articles.author: Mary DellaValle

paras.en: Automotive Parts Headquarters Inc. (APH), together with its supplier partners and the Bartlett family, raised $513,000 through its annual fundraiser benefiting WACOSA, a central Minnesota nonprofit serving adults with disabilities. The 2026 event brings the fundraiser’s 14-year total to $3.7 million.
Proceeds support WACOSA programs that provide meaningful employment, day services and opportunities for more than 650 adults with disabilities across central Minnesota.

The event began with a walleye shore lunch and guided tours of WACOSA before attendees gathered at APH’s newest facility (a bulk storage warehouse) in St. Cloud for a pie and ice cream social celebrating its grand opening and APH’s “Building Our Future Together” initiative.

Attendees also participated in a hands-on art experience led by WACOSA artist-in-residence Dan Mondloch. The individual pieces created during the event will be incorporated into a collaborative collage inspired by the northern lights above a Minnesota lake.

“The day captured so much of what makes this event special,” said Jason Vogel, president of APH Stores Inc. “Bringing our supplier partners, employees and friends together to experience WACOSA’s mission firsthand, celebrate a new chapter for APH and create something together was incredibly rewarding.”

The day concluded with a cocktail reception, lobster-themed dinner and awards ceremony hosted by John and Nancy Bartlett at their home. A highlight of the evening was the presentation of a $513,000 check to Nancy Betts, executive director of WACOSA.

“Fourteen years of support from APH, its supplier partners and the Bartlett family has created a remarkable legacy for the people we serve,” Betts said. “This generosity creates opportunities for people to discover their strengths, contribute to their communities and pursue greater independence. We are deeply grateful for the lasting difference this partnership makes.”
Corey Bartlett, CEO and owner of APH, said the event reflects the generosity and commitment of the automotive aftermarket community.

“Every year, this event reminds us of the extraordinary generosity within the automotive aftermarket,” Bartlett said. “What began as a fundraiser has grown into a lasting partnership between APH, our supplier community and WACOSA. Seeing everyone come together to support the people and mission at the heart of WACOSA is what makes this event so meaningful.”
To view highlights from this year’s event, including the celebration, collaborative art project and messages from industry leaders, visit https://vimeo.com/autopartshq/wacosa26.
